language.descriptionAndroid: Applies to the app, the notification and the quick settings tile.

theme.failed: The appearance could not be saved.

app.sessionExpired: Your session has expired. Please sign in again.
app.refreshFailed: Account information could not be updated just now. Mantel keeps trying.
app.tunnelUpTitle: The VPN tunnel is still active
app.tunnelUpLoggedOut: You are signed out, but the tunnel keeps running. You can disconnect it here at any time.
app.tunnelUpStale: The tunnel no longer responds. Disconnect it to go online without the VPN.
app.alwaysOnHint: “Always-on VPN” is turned on for Mantel: Android tries to restart the tunnel, and with “Block connections without VPN” the device stays offline. Turn it off in the Android settings if you do not want to use Mantel right now.

home.noteFirewallLockdown: Permanent kill switch: internet outside the tunnel is blocked.
home.noteDirect: Your traffic goes straight through your provider.
home.noteKillSwitchWireGuard: Kill switch on. WireGuard blocks everything outside the tunnel, including DNS requests to other servers.
home.noteKillSwitchFirewall: Kill switch via the Windows Firewall. Only your LAN stays reachable outside the tunnel.
home.noteNoKillSwitch: No kill switch. If the tunnel drops, traffic leaves unprotected.
home.noteAndroidLockdown: Android blocks connections without VPN. Without the tunnel you have no internet.
home.noteAndroidKillSwitchLan: Kill switch on. Only your LAN stays reachable outside the tunnel.
home.noteAndroidKillSwitch: Kill switch on. All traffic goes through the tunnel, including DNS.
home.noteAndroidLockdownHint: For protection without the tunnel too: turn on “Block connections without VPN” in the settings.
home.openWifiText: This Wi-Fi is not encrypted. Others on the network can read what you send without the tunnel.
home.staleWarning: No handshake for more than three minutes: the server is not responding, your network blocks UDP or this device was removed. Mantel checks and disconnects if the device is no longer registered.
home.obfuscatedTooltip: WireGuard runs disguised as HTTPS (TLS over TCP 443).
home.blockedLost: The tunnel is gone and the kill switch keeps blocking everything outside it. Reconnect or lift the block.
home.blockedAlwaysOn: The permanent kill switch blocks everything outside the tunnel while you are not connected.
home.blockedLeftover: Kill switch rules are still active although there is no connection.
home.blockedCaptive: Wi-Fi with a sign-in page (hotel, train, café)? Lift the block, sign in in the browser, then reconnect.
home.blockedAndroid: Android blocks connections without VPN. Connect, or turn off “Block connections without VPN” in the Android settings.
home.noAdmin: Without administrator rights Mantel cannot set up a tunnel or firewall rules. Run the app as administrator.
home.noKeystoreAndroid: The Android keystore is not available. Keys are only kept in memory.
home.noKeystoreWindows: Windows encryption (DPAPI) is not available. Keys are only kept in memory.

map.labelOff: World map with {count} locations. Not connected.
map.youTitle: Roughly where you are, estimated from this device's time zone. Never sent anywhere.

locations.title: Choose location
locations.none: No locations are available right now.

reason.paused: Not accepting new devices right now

locations.pageHint: Choose where your traffic enters the internet. If you are connected, Mantel switches right away.

login.title: Sign in
login.invalidLength: An account number has exactly 16 digits.
login.noAccount: Don't have an account number yet?
login.registerRateLimited: Too many new accounts in a short time. Please try again later.
login.firewallActive: The permanent kill switch is on. Apart from Mantel the internet is blocked until you connect or lift it in the tray menu.
login.totpBody: Two-factor authentication is on for this account. Enter the 6-digit code from your authenticator app, or a recovery code.

paid.expiringNote: Renew in time so your protection isn't interrupted.
paid.graceNote: Grace period until {date}. After that, access is locked.
paid.expiredNote: Renew your account to use Mantel again.
paid.newNote: New accounts start without time. Buy time or redeem a voucher on the website, then you can connect.
paid.renewHint: Opens your account on the website. Redeem vouchers there.

settings.connectionDescription: Applied to the tunnel as soon as it is saved.
settings.killSwitchAndroid: While the tunnel is up, all traffic goes through it, including DNS. To block without a tunnel too, see “Protection by Android”.
settings.killSwitchDesktop: Blocks all traffic outside the tunnel, including DNS. Stays in place on location changes and drops until you disconnect.
settings.lanFirewall: Printers and NAS stay reachable. The kill switch then runs through the Windows Firewall.
settings.lanDefault: Printers and NAS stay reachable, LAN addresses don’t go into the tunnel.
settings.ipv6Description: Off means no IPv6 address. IPv6 is still routed into the tunnel, never around it.
settings.deviceKeyDescription: Creates a new key pair on this device. The private key never leaves the device; tunnel IP and port forwarding stay the same, a running connection briefly reconnects.
settings.deviceKeyNoDevice: Connect to a location once, then this device gets its key.
settings.portForwardingDescription: Opens a port on {city} through which this device receives incoming connections. Needed for torrents with full upload and seeding.
settings.portForwardingNoDevice: Connect to a location once, then you can open a port here.
settings.portForwardingHint: In your torrent client, enter this port as the incoming (listening) port, turn off UPnP/NAT-PMP and bind the client to the VPN interface.
settings.portForwardingWarning: The port makes this device reachable from the internet. Keep it on only while you need it, and only for programs you trust.
settings.portForwardingSwitchLocation: Switching location releases the port; switch it on again at the new location.
settings.torDescription: {city} sends all traffic of this device through the Tor network. Switching needs no reconnect.
settings.torNoDevice: Connect to a location once, then Tor can be switched on here.
settings.torUnavailable: {city} does not offer Tor right now.
settings.torLimits: Slower than without Tor. TCP only: games, calls, QUIC and other UDP services do not work, and some sites block Tor.
settings.torOnion: .onion addresses open directly in the browser; some browsers such as Firefox or Chrome partly block them on their own.
settings.torFingerprint: No replacement for Tor Browser: it protects far better against fingerprinting.
settings.torPortForwarding: Port forwarding is off in Tor mode.

portForwardingReasons.unsupported: {city} does not offer port forwarding yet.
portForwardingReasons.disabled: Port forwarding is switched off on {city} right now.
portForwardingReasons.expired: Port forwarding needs an active account.
portForwardingReasons.tor: Not available in Tor mode. An existing port stays reserved.

settings.systemLockdownDescription: The strongest protection comes from Android itself: whenever the tunnel is not up, the system blocks all traffic, even before Mantel has started.
settings.alwaysOnVpnDescription: Android starts Mantel automatically and keeps the connection up.
settings.blockWithoutVpnDescription: Blocks the internet whenever the tunnel is down, even after a crash or restart.
settings.systemLockdownHowTo: Open the VPN settings, tap the gear next to Mantel and turn on “Always-on VPN” and “Block connections without VPN”.
settings.systemLockdownCached: Android only tells while the tunnel is up. Shown is the state from the last connection.
settings.systemLockdownEnableBoth: Tap the gear next to Mantel and turn on both options.
settings.openAndroidSettingsFailed: The Android settings could not be opened.

excludedSome.one: {count} app does not use the tunnel
excludedSome.other: {count} apps do not use the tunnel

settings.disguiseDescription: Only changes the icon and name on the home screen. The app itself stays Mantel.
settings.disguiseLauncherNote: The home screen picks up the new icon after a few seconds. Home screen shortcuts may disappear; add them again from the app drawer.
settings.disguiseVisibleNote: While connected, Android still shows the key icon in the status bar and the Mantel notification. In the Android settings the app is still called Mantel.
settings.alwaysOnDescription: Blocks the internet even when the tunnel is off or the app crashes. Mantel servers, DHCP and, if enabled, your LAN stay allowed.
settings.alwaysOnRowDescription: Lift it at any time from the tray menu or with mantel.exe --disable-killswitch.
settings.alwaysOnConfirm: Without the tunnel you will have no internet. Turn it on?
settings.alwaysOnNeedsAdmin: Mantel needs administrator rights to change this. Run the app as administrator.
settings.dnsDescription: Filtered on the server. The app only stores your selection.
settings.upcomingDescription: Not implemented yet, so they can’t be switched on here.

customPort.label: Custom port
customPort.description: 53 or 443 for networks that filter VPNs.

settings.debugDescription: Debug builds only: server, build, API log, diagnostics.
settings.logoutConfirm: Disconnects the tunnel, removes this device from your account and deletes the local keys.
settings.autoConnectOpenWifiDescription: Connects as soon as this device joins an unencrypted Wi-Fi. Mantel only reads the encryption for this, never the network name.
settings.obfuscationDescription: Disguises WireGuard as HTTPS (TLS, TCP 443) for networks that block VPNs. Auto only uses it when UDP does not get through.
settings.launchAtLoginDescription: Mantel starts minimised to the notification area after you sign in.
settings.connectOnLaunchDescription: Connects to the last chosen location after the automatic start. Only together with the automatic start.
settings.quitActionDescription: What happens to a working connection when you quit Mantel. If the connection is interrupted, Mantel always asks.

states.killSwitchOn: Active, also on drops and location changes

logins.title: Sign-ins
logins.description: When your account is signed in somewhere else, it shows up here until you confirm it. Mantel keeps only the kind of app and the method, no time, no IP address, no location.
logins.bannerBody: Wasn't you? Sign out all other sessions and generate a new account number in the web dashboard.
logins.logoutOthersBody: Every other app and browser using your account is signed out. This app stays signed in.
logins.loggedOutOthers: All other sessions have been signed out.
logins.passkeysBody: Set up passkeys (Face ID, Touch ID, Windows Hello, security key) and two-factor authentication with an authenticator app in the web dashboard under Account. With two-factor authentication on, this app asks for the code when you sign in with your account number.

apps.title: Exclude apps
apps.description: Excluded apps bypass the VPN and use your normal connection. Their traffic is not protected.
apps.lockdownWarning: “Block connections without VPN” is on. Android then usually cuts excluded apps off from the internet.
apps.heading: Apps
apps.noneWithoutSystem: No apps found apart from system apps.
apps.loadFailed: The app list could not be loaded.
apps.excludedLoadFailed: The excluded apps could not be loaded.

wireguard.title: Set up WireGuard for Mantel?
wireguard.body: Mantel builds the tunnel with the official WireGuard for Windows. Mantel can download the files it needs now and keep them for itself. No separate WireGuard app is installed.
wireguard.verified: The file is checked against WireGuard’s signed release list. It is removed again when Mantel is uninstalled.
wireguard.needsAdmin: Mantel needs administrator rights for this. Run the app as administrator.
wireguard.serviceTitle: The Mantel service is not running
wireguard.serviceBody: Tunnel, kill switch and leak protection run in the Windows service “Mantel Service”, so the app itself needs no administrator rights. The service is not responding right now. Repairing it asks Windows for administrator rights once.

dialogs.killSwitchDisabled: Kill switch lifted. The firewall rules have been removed.
dialogs.killSwitchFailed: The kill switch could not be lifted: {reason}
dialogs.quitDetail: It runs as a Windows service and can stay connected without the app, even after a restart. Do you want to stay connected?
dialogs.quitDetailObfuscated: Obfuscation runs inside the app. If you stay connected, the tunnel pauses until the next start (the kill switch keeps blocking); then Mantel reconnects.
dialogs.quitRemember: Don't ask again (can be changed in the settings)
dialogs.quitBlockedMessage: Not connected, but the kill switch blocks the internet.
dialogs.quitBlockedDetail: If you don't disconnect now, the internet stays blocked after quitting until you open Mantel again and connect or disconnect.

register.title: Write it down.
register.body: This is the only time you'll see this number. Keep it in a password manager or on paper.
register.heading: Your account number
register.warning: This number is the only way to sign in. We don't know it; we only store a hash of it. If you lose it, nobody can recover it, not even us.
register.inviteAdded: Invite code applied: {days} days of VPN time added.

debug.title: Debug options
debug.description: Debug builds only. Logs and diagnostics stay on this device.
debug.serverDescription: Set when the app is built (MANTEL_API_URL), cannot be changed in the app.
debug.healthDescription: Calls GET /api/v1/nodes on the configured server.
debug.logDescription: The latest calls, kept in memory only. No bodies, tokens, account numbers, keys or IDs.
debug.tunnelDescription: Live state as the app polls it anyway.
debug.verboseDescription: Writes API calls and tunnel states (without secrets) to the main process console.
debug.copyDiagnosticsDescription: Build, settings, tunnel and API log as text, secrets redacted.
debug.resetDescription: Disconnects, signs out, lifts the kill switch and deletes this build's token, keys and settings.
debug.resetConfirm: Really reset everything? The device is deleted on the server.

update.laterLabel: Hide the notice about version {version} for 3 days
update.requiredBody: This version of Mantel is no longer supported. Download and install the new version to connect again.
update.connectedNotice: Your current connection stays up until you disconnect. Connecting again needs the update.
update.failed: Can't reach the update server right now.

pq.settingDescription: Additional key exchange with ML-KEM-768. Protects recorded traffic against later decryption by quantum computers. Connecting takes a little longer.
pq.reconnectNote: An existing connection is re-established for this.
pq.lockdownHint: Without “Block connections without VPN”, traffic of other apps can briefly bypass the VPN while switching to quantum protection.
pq.badgeTooltip: This tunnel additionally uses a key agreed with ML-KEM-768.
pq.actionTurnOffHint: Turns off “Quantum-resistant tunnel” on this device and connects with classic WireGuard.
pq.actionsLabel: Options after the quantum-resistant tunnel error

support.title: Support
support.hint: Write to us when something does not work. We answer here.
support.e2e: End-to-end encrypted: only you and the Mantel team can read the messages.
support.empty: No tickets yet. If you have a question or a problem, just open one.
support.unavailable: Support is not set up yet. Please try again later.
support.otherDeviceHint: This ticket was created on another device. Open Support there once, then it shows up here too.
support.undecryptable: This message could not be decrypted.
support.messagePlaceholder: Briefly describe what happened. Please do not include your account number.
support.closedHint: This ticket is closed. Reopen it to answer.

manage.proxiesSummary: SOCKS5 and HTTP on the Mantel servers

devices.title: Devices
devices.description: All devices of your account. Each has its own WireGuard key and belongs to one location.
devices.empty: A device is created when you connect for the first time.
devices.nameHint: At most {max} characters. When you switch location, the apps create a new device with a new name.
devices.removeDescription: The device loses access right away. Its forwarded ports are released.
devices.removeOwnDescription: This is this device: the connection is ended. The app creates a new device the next time you connect. You stay signed in.

forwards.title: Port forwarding
forwards.description: Opens ports on a device's location; incoming connections (TCP and UDP) go to exactly that device. Needed for torrents with full upload and seeding.
forwards.empty: Forwarded ports belong to a device. Connect once, then you can open ports here.
forwards.noForward: This device has no tunnel the server can forward to.
forwards.limitNote: At most {max} per device. The server does not allow more at the moment.
forwards.hint: In your torrent program, enter the port as the incoming (listening) port, turn off UPnP/NAT-PMP and bind the program to the VPN interface.
forwards.warning: An open port makes the device reachable from the internet. Keep ports open only while you need them.
forwards.switchNote: When the device switches location, it gets a new port and the old one is released.
forwards.localPortHelp: The port your program listens on, e.g. 3000. Leave empty to use the public port.
forwards.localPortInvalid: Enter a whole number from 1 to 65535.
forwards.listenHint: The program on your device must listen on 0.0.0.0 (all interfaces), not only on 127.0.0.1.

proxies.title: Proxies
proxies.description: SOCKS5 or HTTP proxies on the Mantel servers, with their own port and password. For programs or devices that can't use a VPN.
proxies.empty: A proxy runs on a location of your choice. Traffic leaves it through Tor or the Mantel IP.
proxies.soon: Proxies on the Mantel servers arrive with one of the next server updates.
proxies.info: Tor is much slower and changes the IP. SOCKS5 and HTTP send the username and password unencrypted: for anything sensitive use them only over a VPN connection or with HTTPS destinations.

exitHints.tor: Leaves through Tor, changing IP, slower.
exitHints.direct: Leaves with the location's IP, fast.

proxies.credentialsOnce: The password is shown only now. Save it before you close this window.
proxies.removeDescription: Programs using these credentials lose their connection right away.
proxies.telegramInfo: Add the proxy to Telegram with this link. Anyone with the link can use it; "New link" makes the old one stop working.

mac.helperTitle: Set up the helper for the tunnel?
mac.helperBody: On the Mac a small helper builds the tunnel, sets routes and DNS and switches the kill switch. macOS asks for your admin password once for this. WireGuard is already inside, there is nothing else to install.
mac.helperNote: The helper only accepts requests from your user account, checks each of them and runs no other commands. After a Mantel update it is set up again here.
mac.helperPrompt: Mantel wants to set up the helper for the VPN tunnel.
mac.noHelper: The helper is not responding. Without it Mantel cannot set up a tunnel or the kill switch.
mac.noKeychain: The macOS keychain is not available. Keys are kept in memory only.
mac.alwaysOnNeedsHelper: Mantel needs the helper to change this.
mac.alwaysOnRowDescription: Lift it any time from the Mantel icon in the menu bar or in Terminal: sudo {command} disable-killswitch --flavor {flavor}
mac.lanFirewall: Printers and NAS stay reachable. The kill switch then uses the macOS packet filter (pf).
mac.quitDetail: It runs in the Mantel helper and can stay connected without the app, even after a restart. Do you want to stay connected?
mac.killSwitchDisabled: Kill switch lifted. The pf rules were removed.
mac.launchAtLoginDescription: Mantel starts minimised to the menu bar after you log in.
